validated_work_order.understanding:
#25 bundles four follow-ups the review of PR #23 (for #7) found and deliberately did not fix there. I re-checked all four against the current tree; three still hold and one has evaporated.

Finding 1 — mergeTransactions drops schedule_occurrence (still reproduces, and it is the real bug). Both db.updateTransaction payloads in mergeTransactionsNoTransfer (merge.ts:165 split branch, merge.ts:176 normal branch) copy `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule` but say nothing about the stamp. I drove it with a probe on current main: created a recurring schedule (next_date 2016-12-02), posted it via schedulesApp.handlers['schedule/post-transaction'], inserted an identical-amount transaction dated 2016-11-12, merged them. Before: posted row {id6, date 2016-12-02, schedule id3, schedule_occurrence 2016-12-02}. After: kept row {id7, date 2016-11-12, schedule id3, schedule_occurrence null} and getHasTransactionsQuery matched 0 rows. The occurrence reads as unpaid again — the exact regression #7 exists to close.

Finding 2 — the migration file has no trailing newline (still reproduces). `tail -c 1 ...1790969762045_add_schedule_occurrence_to_transactions.sql | xxd` returns 00000000: 3b; the sibling 1759842823172_add_isGlobal_to_preferences.sql returns 00000000: 0a.

Finding 3 — transfer mirror legs are never stamped (still reproduces, currently inert). addTransfer builds its mirror-leg object at transfer.ts:68 with `schedule: transaction.schedule` and no stamp; updateTransfer writes the mirror at transfer.ts:131 with the same omission. My probe confirms the mirror comes out schedule_occurrence null while the main leg carries 2016-12-02. The reviewer is right that this does NOT currently re-open the bug — every consumer of getHasTransactionsQuery collapses to a Set of schedule ids or a boolean (schedules/app.ts:602, :654, useSchedules.ts:34), so an extra matching row cannot change an outcome. Latent trap, not a live defect, and the same one-line fix.

Finding 4 — snapshot churn — does not hold up, and I am dropping it. The reviewer's own evidence says it is a @@ context-window artefact, verified against main, "no code change is required"; the remedy was one sentence in a PR that is now merged. Its concern is carried forward instead as AC-5 plus the explicit instruction that the new transfer test must not use snapshots.

No decisions were recorded for this issue (plan/brief.md records none), so nothing here overrides anything.

This version exists to answer one objection to v1. The review held that AC-4 and AC-5 carried verify: "test" but named no tests[] case and appeared in no qa_script step, so no stage ever executed them. That was correct: a command written only in how_to_verify is not run by anything. v2 leaves the diagnosis and the diff unchanged — every claim is re-verified, not inherited — and fixes the execution path. qa_script now ends with a step QA runs verbatim (new step 9) that prints the migration's last byte, diffs the snapshot directory against the PR base and requires empty output, and confirms the node suite was green with no -u. AC-4 and AC-5 both name that step. AC-4 additionally stops claiming a test proves it: no test asserts a file's last byte, and writing one would test the filesystem, not the code.
validated_work_order.root_cause: `schedule` and `schedule_occurrence` were introduced as a pair by #7, but #7 only ever taught the WRITE that creates a stamped row (schedules/app.ts:572). Every pre-existing write that copies an existing transaction's schedule onto another row was left untouched, so the two fields can drift apart: a row can end up schedule-linked with no occurrence identity. `db.updateTransaction` drops `undefined` fields (schema-helpers.ts:136) and keeps `null`, which is why these paths silently leave the stamp at its existing value instead of erroring.
validated_work_order.approach:
One rule, applied at every place that copies a transaction's schedule onto another row: the occurrence stamp travels with the schedule link, or not at all.

I audited every write that propagates `schedule` from one transaction to another — the audit #7's work order skipped, since it enumerated only the READ paths. There are exactly four, and all four are in this change: merge.ts:165 (split branch of mergeTransactionsNoTransfer), merge.ts:176 (normal branch), transfer.ts:68 (addTransfer, constructing the mirror leg), transfer.ts:131 (updateTransfer, updating the mirror leg).

Two other sites carry `schedule` and are deliberately NOT touched. transfer.ts:83 and :89 write `matchedSchedule` back onto the SAME transaction whose stamp is already correct — nothing is copied between rows. forecast-schedules.ts:273 copies `schedule` onto a simulated transfer leg, but that leg is never persisted (it exists only in the forecast's in-memory simulatedTransactions) and its sourceTransaction is built six lines earlier at :218 with no stamp to copy. find-schedules.ts:29's `schedule: null` is a query filter, not a write.

On the merge expression I specify `??` rather than the `||` used on the line above. A stamp is either a positive YYYYMMDD integer or null, so the two operators agree on every reachable value; `??` states "take the dropped row's only when the kept row has none" without implying that 0 is a meaningful date. It is a deliberate difference from the surrounding line and the reviewer should see it as one.

On updateTransfer I specify `transaction.schedule_occurrence` verbatim rather than `?? null`, and this is load-bearing. conform() drops undefined from an update (schema-helpers.ts:136) but writes null, so a partial update that omits the field leaves the mirror alone — exactly how the schedule line above it already behaves — while an explicit null from the client clears the stamp alongside the schedule link. I verified all three of those behaviours with the probe rather than reasoning about them: after the fix, a full update leaves the mirror stamped at 20161202, a partial update that omits the field leaves it stamped at 20161202, and an explicit null clears it to null. `?? null` would have wiped the mirror's stamp on every partial API update that never mentioned it.

The migration fix is a one-byte append. Migrations are keyed by filename, not content, so an already-migrated database is unaffected.

No release note: the behaviour this corrects was introduced by #7, whose note (upcoming-release-notes/keep-posted-schedules-paid-today.md) is still unreleased. Fixing it before it ships needs no second note.

files.change:
In BOTH db.updateTransaction payloads inside mergeTransactionsNoTransfer — the split branch (line 165, `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule,` closing with `} as unknown as TransactionEntity)`) and the normal branch (line 176, closing with `} as TransactionEntity)`) — add one line immediately after the existing schedule line:

      schedule_occurrence: keep.schedule_occurrence ?? drop.schedule_occurrence,

Both branches are named by the review and both need it; a fix to only the normal branch leaves the split path broken. `??` is deliberate — see approach. Keep the existing casts unchanged; TransactionEntity.schedule_occurrence is `string | null | undefined` so the value type-checks against the optional field with no cast change. I applied both lines and `yarn typecheck` passed all 10 projects.
files.why: Finding 1 — the one finding that re-opens the bug #7 closed. Reproduced by me on current main: matching rows went 1 -> 0 after a merge, and 0 -> 1 with the fix.

files.change:
Two additions, each one line, each placed immediately after the existing `schedule: transaction.schedule,` it belongs beside:

1. In the transferTransaction object literal in addTransfer (line 68), add `schedule_occurrence: transaction.schedule_occurrence,` so the auto-created mirror leg inherits the main leg's occurrence identity. It reaches the insert via the existing `db.insertTransaction({ ...transferTransaction, notes, cleared, schedule: matchedSchedule })` spread at line 74 — do not add it to that call site separately.
2. In the db.updateTransaction payload in updateTransfer (line 131), add `schedule_occurrence: transaction.schedule_occurrence,`.

Pass the value through verbatim in both places. Do NOT write `?? null`: conform() drops undefined from an update but writes null, so a partial update that omits the field must leave the mirror alone — which is precisely how the schedule line above behaves. `?? null` would wipe the mirror's stamp on any partial API update that never mentioned it. Verified by probe with the fix applied: full update -> mirror stamped 20161202; partial update omitting the field -> still 20161202; explicit null -> cleared.
files.why: Finding 3 — currently inert (all consumers of getHasTransactionsQuery collapse to a Set or a boolean) but the latent trap the reviewer flagged.
Finding 2 — the repo's own additive-migration convention.

cases: carries the occurrence stamp from the dropped transaction when the kept transaction has none — mirrors the existing case at line 300, 'preserves schedule link from dropped transaction when kept transaction has none': t1 banksynced and unstamped (the keep), t2 stamped with a schedule and a schedule_occurrence (the drop); after the merge the single surviving row has both `schedule` and `schedule_occurrence` equal to t2's

keeps the kept transaction's own stamp when both rows carry one — t1 (keep) stamped for 'schedule-keep', t2 (drop) stamped for 'schedule-drop'; the surviving row must carry t1's schedule AND t1's schedule_occurrence, so the stamp and the schedule link never disagree
preserves the kept transaction's stamp when the dropped row has none — guards against the new line clobbering an existing stamp with undefined

carries the occurrence stamp in the split branch — the branch at merge.ts:165 is a different db.updateTransaction call and needs its own case: keep is a plain banksynced transaction, drop is a stamped split parent with children; after the merge the kept row must have gained schedule, schedule_occurrence and is_parent
every case asserts on the id mergeTransactions returns rather than by position, which is what the existing tests in this block already do

the mirror leg carries the schedule and occurrence stamp of its main leg — insert a transaction with a schedule, a schedule_occurrence and a transfer payee, call transfer.onInsert, then read the mirror with a plain db.all against v_transactions and assert it has the same schedule AND the same schedule_occurrence as the main leg. Assert on rows, never on expectSnapshotWithDiffer — see AC-5

the stamp survives an update of the main leg — re-read the main leg so the payload carries its real transfer_id (this is what routes onUpdate to updateTransfer rather than a second addTransfer), change the main leg's date, call transfer.onUpdate, and assert the mirror still carries both fields

a partial update that omits the field leaves the mirror's stamp alone — call onUpdate with the main leg's fields minus schedule_occurrence and assert the mirror's stamp is unchanged. This is the case that makes `?? null` wrong: conform() drops undefined but writes null, so `?? null` would silently clear the mirror here
clearing the schedule link on the main leg clears the stamp on the mirror too — assert a main leg sent with `schedule: null, schedule_occurrence: null` leaves the mirror with both null

merging a posted occurrence into an earlier duplicate does not un-pay the schedule — inside the existing `describe('occurrence stamp')` block at line 1150, which already has createRecurringSchedule, postTransaction, readMatches and the NEXT_DATE fixture: post an occurrence, insert an identical-amount transaction dated earlier (pass the date as a plain '2016-11-12' string to db.insertTransaction — toDateRepr is for db.update, and passing it to an insert throws `Invalid date`), call mergeTransactions([{ id: postedId }, { id: duplicateId }]), then assert (a) the id mergeTransactions returns has schedule_occurrence equal to NEXT_DATE, and (b) readMatches(scheduleId) returns exactly one row. Before this fix (b) is 0 — I measured both, and 1 after. The dropped row is tombstoned rather than physically deleted, so do not assert on raw SELECT * FROM transactions counts, which include tombstones

qa_script: Bring the app up (`yarn start`, or `yarn start:server-dev`), open a budget with 'View demo' so there is real data to merge against.

Schedules page: create a recurring schedule — a name, a fixed amount (e.g. 100 out), a monthly date condition on a specific day. Post its current occurrence with the schedule's post/Pay action. Confirm the schedule now reads as paid for that occurrence.
In that account's register, manually add a second transaction with the SAME amount dated roughly three weeks EARLIER than the posted one. It must be the identical amount — merge refuses a mismatch.
Select exactly those two rows and use Merge. Confirm one row survives and still carries the schedule link.
Reload and return to the Schedules page. The occurrence must still read as paid. Before this fix it flips back to 'Due' and the upcoming row comes back — that flip is the bug.

Transfer leg (expected to be a no-op on screen, confirm it stays one): take a schedule-posted transaction and change its payee to another account's transfer payee. A mirror row appears in the other account. Nothing may duplicate, disappear, or change the schedule's paid status.
Repeat step 6 by editing the main leg's date afterwards. The mirror must still track it and the schedule must still read as paid.
No new console errors, and no new rows in either account's register beyond the expected mirror.

Mechanical checks — run all three and require each to pass before reporting QA green. (a) MIGRATION NEWLINE: `tail -c 1 packages/loot-core/migrations/1790969762045_add_schedule_occurrence_to_transactions.sql | xxd` must print `00000000: 0a`; it prints `00000000: 3b` on unmodified main, so this is a real check, not a tautology. (b) NO SNAPSHOT CHURN: `git diff --stat "$(git merge-base HEAD main)" -- packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/__snapshots__/` must print nothing at all. (c) SUITE GREEN, NO `-u`: run `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node` with NO `-u` flag and confirm it reports 1212 passed / 2 skipped / 87 files with no snapshot written. Steps (a) and (b) are the execution path for AC-4 and AC-5, which no test case covers and which nothing else in this script would have run.
risks: The merge change means a kept row can acquire a stamp it did not have, sourced from the dropped row. The invariant that makes this safe is that stamp and schedule link are written by the SAME expression, so they can never disagree: `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule` picks keep's schedule whenever keep has one, and in that case keep necessarily has a meaningful stamp or none at all. If a future edit ever decouples those two lines the invariant breaks, so keep them adjacent.

The transfer change means two rows can now match the same occurrence. Every consumer of getHasTransactionsQuery collapses to a Set of schedule ids or a boolean — schedules/app.ts:602, schedules/app.ts:654, desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts:34 — so an additional matching row cannot change any of their outcomes. I read all three; none counts rows.

forecast-schedules.ts:273 propagates `schedule` to a simulated transfer leg without a stamp and is deliberately left alone. It is not a write path — the row is never persisted — but a future change that persists forecast rows would have to revisit it.

QA step 9's command (b) uses `git merge-base HEAD main` rather than a literal ref, because the branch under test may not be called main and QA may be on a detached HEAD. If main does not resolve the command fails loudly rather than silently diffing against the wrong base — that is the safe direction.

No new hosts, no network calls, no new dependencies. Nothing in this change touches a forbidden_paths entry: packages/loot-core/migrations/** is not among them (only packages/ci-actions/src/migrations/**, packages/loot-core/src/mocks/migrations/** and packages/loot-core/src/server/migrate/** are), so the migration edit is permitted.

alternatives_considered.approach: Cover AC-4 and AC-5 with test cases instead of qa_script steps (e.g. a node test that reads the migration's last byte, and a test that shells out to `git diff` on the snapshot directory).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This was the substance of the v1 objection and it is right that those criteria had no execution path — but a shell-out test is a worse execution path. It couples the unit suite to git state and to the working directory, it fails on a shallow clone or a detached HEAD where the diff base cannot be resolved, and it would run on every future commit for a property already enforced by .nano-staged on every commit in this repo. qa_script is where a repository-level invariant belongs: QA runs it verbatim at the end of the pass, and a red line there fails the ticket.

alternatives_considered.approach: Clear the stamp whenever the schedule link is cleared (a shared helper or an invariant enforced in db/aql), rather than copying the stamp at each of the four write paths.

The merge bug is not a missing clear, it is a missing copy: keep.schedule and drop.schedule are different values and the code already merges them by hand. A guard that only enforces 'no stamp without a schedule' would have prevented neither the merge nor the transfer mirror leg.

alternatives_considered.approach: Write `schedule_occurrence: keep.schedule_occurrence || drop.schedule_occurrence`, matching the `||` on the line above.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Equivalent on every reachable value (a stamp is a positive YYYYMMDD integer or null, so 0 and '' cannot occur), but `??` states the intent precisely. Kept `??` and flagged the deliberate difference from the surrounding line so a reviewer reads it as a choice.

assumptions: `schedule_occurrence` can only ever be null or a positive YYYYMMDD integer (the migration declares it INTEGER and #7 writes schedule.next_date through it), so `??` and `||` behave identically here and no falsy-but-valid stamp exists.

The desktop client sends a whole transaction entity on edit, so transaction.schedule_occurrence is present when the UI updates a schedule-posted transaction. This is why updateTransfer can pass the value through verbatim; a caller that sends only `{ id, notes }` leaves the mirror's stamp alone — the intended-and-safe direction, which I verified with the probe rather than assuming.

db.getTransaction returns rows read back through the AQL schema, so keep.schedule_occurrence / drop.schedule_occurrence are null rather than undefined for an unstamped row — either way `??` treats them the same.

Merges of two transactions that are each stamped for DIFFERENT schedules already pick one schedule (`keep.schedule || drop.schedule`); this change makes the stamp follow that same pick, rather than introducing a new selection rule.

`date` on a db.insertTransaction call is a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' string. I hit this myself: passing toDateRepr(...) to an insert throws `Invalid date` from convertInputType (schema-helpers.ts:30), because toDateRepr is only right for the db.update path. The implementer will otherwise lose a cycle to it, so the app.test.ts case names it.

Already true of the `schedule` field on the same line; recorded as a residual risk rather than adding a condition the review did not ask for.

Whether QA's checkout will resolve a `main` ref for the merge-base in step 9(b). I wrote the command to fail loudly rather than diff the wrong tree, but I cannot know the shape of QA's checkout from here.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: No council ran on this replan. The only decision in front of me was the v1 plan review's single objection, that AC-4 and AC-5 carried verify:"test" with no tests[] case and no qa_script step and therefore had no execution path. I agreed with it — a command written only in how_to_verify is run by nothing — and fixed it by adding qa_script step 9, which names all three commands verbatim (migration last byte, snapshot-directory diff, suite green with no -u) and which AC-4 and AC-5 now point at by step number. Nothing else in v1 was contested, so I kept its diagnosis and diff rather than re-deriving them, but re-verified every claim independently instead of inheriting v1's evidence: findings 1 and 3 reproduced from scratch with new probes, finding 2 read off the byte, the fix re-probed, and the full node suite and typecheck run green. The one thing v1 got wrong that I corrected on the merits is AC-4's shape: v1 marked it verify:"test" as though a test proved it, when the honest statement is that no test does and QA's step 9(a) is what runs it.
residual_risks: In addTransfer, runRules may assign a different schedule to the mirror leg than the main leg's (`matchedSchedule = schedule ?? transaction.schedule`). The stamp is copied unconditionally alongside it, so in that (unverified) case the mirror would carry a schedule and a stamp that belong to different schedules. Pre-existing behaviour of the `schedule` field on the same object; the guard, if one is ever wanted, belongs on both fields together.

AC-4 and AC-5 are enforced at QA time by commands, not by CI. A future change could reintroduce either without any test failing — a missing trailing newline or a stray -u in a contributor's local run would pass the suite. A deliberate trade for not coupling the unit suite to the filesystem and to git state, but it does mean the guarantee is only as good as whoever runs qa_script step 9.
